page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.large is a storage-optimized server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 2 vCPUs, consisting of 1 physical core supporting 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture CPU is equipped with a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

A defining characteristic of the i7ie.large is its bundled local storage, which consists of a 1250 GB NVMe SSD. This high-capacity local storage is paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this instance configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a significant contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench with a score of 2289.0, alongside strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression at 34.71 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.08 GB/sec. However, due to its low core count, multi-core benchmarks are limited, with stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the poor and weak categories, respectively. Memory bandwidth also shows constraints, with large block read-only bandwidth at 22.06 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 23.35 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7ie.large offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage and DDR5 memory relative to its small CPU footprint, making it a specialized option for workloads that require fast local storage but do not demand massive parallel compute power. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight database operations, local caching, and storage-heavy workloads that benefit from high-speed local NVMe drives.

A key highlight is its bundled 1250 GB NVMe SSD local storage, paired with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This profile makes the i7ie.large qualitatively cost-efficient for storage-intensive applications requiring high-speed local NVMe capacity without heavy multi-threaded compute requirements, such as lightweight databases, caching layers, and single-threaded data processing.
